summary: vps-bootstrap.sh: ALTER TABLE OWNER TO guru for app tables (defensive ownership reset)
description:
Tables in the live guru DB are split-owned: some by 'guru' (the DB owner role), some by 'postgres' (probably from earlier migrations that ran as sudo -u postgres without SET ROLE guru). Symptom on PR #27's deploy: 'must be owner of table users' / 'must be owner of table sessions' on every CREATE INDEX, transaction rolls back, migrations effectively no-op.

Two-part fix:

1. One-shot reset on the live VPS (operator):
     sudo -u postgres psql -d guru -c "REASSIGN OWNED BY postgres TO guru"
   (or table-by-table ALTER TABLE OWNER TO guru for surgical control).

2. Defensive ownership reset baked into vps-bootstrap.sh's step_postgres
   (or a new step_app_db_ownership step) so a fresh setup never ends up
   in this state. Idempotent — already-owned-by-guru is a no-op.

Done when:
- vps-bootstrap.sh runs REASSIGN OWNED BY postgres TO guru (or equivalent) after creating the guru role / DB
- Step is idempotent
- deploy/README.md documents the one-time fix for existing VPSes
- Optional: deploy.sh smoke-checks ownership before migrations and warns if drift is detected

resolution.note: step_postgres now ALTERs any non-guru-owned table in public to guru (idempotent DO block). Existing VPSes need a one-shot of the same SQL — documented in README.
